title: Steam boiler drum control
goal: A boiler engineer can trace main steam, feedwater, safety relief, and the three-element level-control instruments.

rubric.must: The drum visibly connects to a main-steam line through FT-401E and a feedwater line through FT-402E and LV-401.
LT-401, FT-401, and FT-402 are all visibly shown with loop signals around the feedwater control arrangement.
LIC-401 visibly connects to LV-401 by a pneumatic command line.
LV-401 visibly shows diaphragm actuation and FC fail position.
XV-401 is visibly in series on the main steam path downstream of the steam flow element.
PSV-401 is visibly connected to the drum steam space.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: Codex visual recheck: the slash-marked pneumatic signal leaves the left edge of LIC-401, runs left to its riser, steps farther left above the drum, then descends to the LV-401 diaphragm actuator. It is continuous and visually distinguishable from the nearby PSV-401 relief piping; the feedwater and steam paths remain traceable.

items.evidence: D-401 visibly connects rightward through FE-401 to the steam line and downward through LV-401 and FE-402 to the feedwater header.
LT-401, FT-401, and FT-402 are all visible, with dashed loop signal lines shown around LIC-401, FIC-402, and the feedwater control arrangement.

Codex visual recheck: the slash-marked pneumatic signal leaves the left edge of LIC-401, runs left to its riser, steps farther left above the drum, then descends to the LV-401 diaphragm actuator. It is continuous and visually distinguishable from the nearby PSV-401 relief piping; the feedwater and steam paths remain traceable.
LV-401 visibly has a diaphragm actuator and an adjacent FC marking.
XV-401 is visibly installed in series downstream of FE-401 on the line to STEAM HEADER.
PSV-401 is visibly connected by a DN50 branch to the top steam space of D-401, with discharge toward TO ATM.
